[b]Pre Chimor History[/b]
Before Tacaynamo do founding Chanchán, even before the Waqas qhapacs, the old khipus tell us about the period when our nation was split in two people, the so called "Kacán and Tingát" were two nations that ruled, existing since 650 years before the Waqas arriving to rule the land.
[b]Tingát[/b] .
The Tingát were a kingdom covering from the limits of Pacatnamú to even further from Chimor western limits, it spoke a language that is believed to be ancestor of Chimuan Languages and Ichma languages, called proto Chimor, it capital was centralized in Limaq, a city that exist until today but after the kingdom  fall, it lose it shine.
Tingát was ruled by a high social class called Mawa, it did not had a central ruler, instead, being rules by the Mawa class of priests and clergy, while the kingdom was divided into several lords, similar to "fiefs", called a "Saya" for the coastal lords, and "Wanqas" for the non coastal.
The Tingát were the first to introduze the Mitma, called by them as "Mita", and every group of mitma'ed who were sent to work, were forced to build a monument with their names.
In Limaq, they had an ancient temple, called Waqayamay, which every mawa were mummified and prepared, about 100 mummies of women and men were found in the temple , in the same temple, there was a Scyther Waqa figure, called Supay, perhaps the god of death.
They collapsed around the same time as the Kacán, around the 5th century, as [i]The kingdoms fallen 100 years before the Waqas qhapac horizon.[/i]
[i] Tingát was organized , but ruled by a minority, and when the majority revolted, the Mawas were exterminate, burials desecrated, and mummies pierced and sliced, after that,  each lord and tformed their own kingdom and tribes, the only left Mawas formed the Irma Civilization, and the lowest class forged their own path.[/i]

[b] Kacán.[/b]
Believed to be nothing but the union of Chiripas, Diakit, and the Punko into a triple alliance, which did not had a single capital, but three capitals, and three Titakins(kings), they would participated an [i]Ahao[/i], or assembly, to keep the alliance each year.
Due the jungles, the Architecture were limited, each city was indeed, the union of several settlements, into a called [i]Gasta[/i], if it were not by the resistance and ferocity of the Kacán alliance, they would be integrated and conquered by the Tingát.
The fall of Kacán alliance happened right after the Tingát fall, since their rival were no longer, the Kacán alliance collapsed and their leaders now could forge their own paths.
